text:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a mismatch between raw token counts emitted by the inference edge and what ends up in the billing ledger after microbatching. Looks like microbatches are being rounded at aggregation and we're losing fractional tokens in the rollup. Anyone seen this?

anita: hmm, can you paste an example? are these partial tokens from streaming responses or from chunked requests?

mike: Streaming responses. Example: edge emits three events for a single request as partial chunks with token_counts: [23, 18, 9] = total 50. Microbatch aggregator groups 10 requests and applies integer rounding per-request to save size, so we end up with sum(round(23/10)+round(18/10)+round(9/10)) across the batch vs summing first. Effectively we lost ~4 tokens on that batch.

ryan: ah yeah that rounding strategy was to keep event size small for the compact ledger. We rounded per-item to a short int and stored a batch-level multiplier. Probably introduced quantization error.

lisa: can we switch to storing per-request integer token counts (int32) and compress the batch payload instead of per-item rounding? storage cost vs accuracy tradeoff.

mike: that's one option. Another is to push exact raw counts to a separate "audit" stream (compressed protobuf) that we keep for N days for reconciliations, and keep the compact stream for quick billing.

anita: we already have an audit topic for long tail errors, but it's consumer-land — not all pipelines subscribe. If we add an audit stream it should be write-once and immutable and tied to provenance ids.

ryan: sketch of a minimal schema (proto-ish):

```
message MeterEvent {
  string request_id = 1;          // provenance id
  string model = 2;
  int64 timestamp = 3;
  repeated int32 chunk_token_counts = 4; // exact per-chunk counts
  int32 total_tokens = 5;         // precomputed exact sum
  map<string,string> provenance = 6; // e.g. edge_id, region
}
```

ryan: If we persist total_tokens exact and chunk_token_counts only to audit topic, compact billing topic can keep only total_tokens and billing tags. That avoids batch-level rounding.

mike: two main concerns: (1) throughput — audit topic size will jump, (2) replay reconciliation — need stable keys so backfills produce deterministic aggregates.

lisa: for throughput we can gzip protocol buffers and use schema evolution with snappy on the audit topic. And we should partition by tenant+day to keep backfills bounded.

anita: on deterministic aggregation: we must ensure the ingestion idempotency key is request_id (not message_id). When we replay we dedupe by request_id, sum total_tokens. Also need to be careful about late-arriving corrections for streaming (edits).

mike: true. We currently have a handshake where edge sets request_id and a sequence_number for chunks. If we record both seq and total_tokens in audit, reconciliation can detect partial vs final. Example flow: edge emits chunk events with seq=1..n and final=true on last chunk. Aggregator should ignore interim events for billing until final=true OR accept interim but only reconcile when final appears.

ryan: that matches my preference: accept interim for near-real-time metrics but mark them provisional. Billing writing must only happen on final confirmation event. We already tag events with provisional=true in the compact topic.

lisa: fine, but customers complained about seeing provisional tokens in the dashboard. We need a flag in the API and console that shows provisional vs settled usage.

anita: ops question: how long do we keep audit topic retention? 90 days? 180? For regulatory reconciliations maybe 365. That impacts storage cost vs the need to reconstruct exact ledgers.

mike: proposal: audit topic retention 365 days compressed, compact billing topic 30 days. Archive old audits to cold storage (S3) beyond 180 days but keep indexing metadata for quick lookup.

ryan: sounds reasonable. Also: add a periodic reconciliation job that compares compact sums vs audit sums back to last-month window and emits anomalies. If discrepancy > X tokens or > Y% we trigger manual review.

anita: thresholds should be per-tenant and global. Small tenants will get noisy percentages otherwise. Use absolute token threshold floor + percentage.

lisa: operational detail — need to update exporter that uploads to the billing ledger to use total_tokens from event and ignore provisional flagged events. We'll also need a migration for events already in compact topic — probably run a backfill that reads audit topic and rewrites compact totals for last 60 days.

mike: backfill plan: 1) run audit->recompute sums by request_id for 60d window; 2) produce corrective delta events to billing-reconciler topic with idempotency keys; 3) notify accounting and mark window as reconciled.

billing-bot: Reminder: run reconciliation job in dry-run mode first. Use --dry-run to produce report only (no ledger writes).

ryan: implementation tasks I can take: update edge SDK to include final flag + ensure stable request_id generation; update meter producer to write exact total_tokens to compact topic (no rounding) and full chunk list to audit topic compressed.

anita: I'll own retention policy + backfill orchestration and the reconciliation thresholds. Will sync with accounting for SLA on reconciled windows.

mike: thanks. Action items summarized: 
- ryan: edge SDK + producer changes (PR)
- anita: retention, backfill plan, reconciliation thresholds
- lisa: console UI flag for provisional/settled usage
- billing-bot: schedule dry-run reconciliation after prod deploy

mike: cool. Let's try to have the PRs and a dry-run report in two weeks. :thumbsup:
